prompt_text: I need braces or Invisalign in Columbus. Which specific orthodontists should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best orthodontist in Columbus Ohio for braces or Invisalign?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific names, but first a couple quick questions so I pick the best matches:
- Do you mean Columbus, Ohio (or another Columbus)?
- Is this for you or a child/teen?
- Do you have dental insurance, a budget, or scheduling preferences (evenings/weekends)?
If you want, give a ZIP and I’ll look up 3–5 local offices with phone numbers and short reasons to call each.

If you’d like to move forward now, here’s a practical plan and the exact people/types to call — and why each matters.

Who to call (quick categories and why)
1. A high-volume Invisalign provider (Platinum/Top/Elite)
   - Why: lots of experience with aligners, predictable ClinCheck planning, they often do many adult cases and know how to manage attachments, refinements, and compliance issues.
   - How to find them: use Align Technology’s “Find a Doctor” (Invisalign provider locator) or Google “Invisalign provider Columbus OH” and look for “Platinum/Elite” badges and many patient before/after photos.

2. A board-certified orthodontist in private practice (AAO member)
   - Why: board-certified or AAO-member orthodontists have completed residency training in orthodontics and follow specialty standards. Good for straightforward to complex cases and long-term follow-up.
   - How to find them: American Association of Orthodontists “Find an Orthodontist” or Google Maps; check reviews and photos.

3. The Ohio State University College of Dentistry — Graduate Orthodontics Clinic (if Columbus, OH)
   - Why: faculty-supervised resident clinics deliver up-to-date care at lower cost; good for complex cases and people on a tighter budget.
   - Note: longer appointment times and treatment supervised by residents/attendings.

4. A pediatric orthodontist (for kids/teens)
   - Why: if the patient is a child or young teen, pediatric specialists are used to growth-modification appliances and interceptive care.

5. A multi-location group with flexible hours / in-network insurance partners
   - Why: if you need weekend/evening appointments, easy transfers between offices, or easy billing for insurance.

Questions to ask when you call (so you can compare apples to apples)
- Are you an Invisalign provider? If yes, what is your provider tier (Gold/Platinum/Elite)? How many cases do you treat per year?
- Are you board-certified in orthodontics? How many years have you been practicing as an orthodontist?
- Do you offer free consultation? If not, what is the exam fee?
- What treatment options do you offer for my need (Invisalign, braces, clear braces, lingual)?
- What is your estimated price range and what does that include (retainers, refinements, x‑rays, emergencies)?
- Average treatment time and number of visits for Invisalign vs braces?
- Do you use digital scanning (iTero) and provide a ClinCheck or simulation before starting?
- Payment plans, insurance acceptance, and third-party financing options?
- Emergency coverage? After-hours contact?
- Can I see before/after photos of similar cases and patient references or online reviews?

What I’d recommend you call first
- The top Invisalign/clear-aligner office in your ZIP (high-volume provider)
- One highly rated private orthodontist who is AAO/board-certified
- OSU Graduate Orthodontics Clinic (if Columbus, OH) for a lower-cost option and second opinion

Typical costs and timelines (ballpark)
- Invisalign: $3,000–$7,500 depending on complexity. Treatment 6–24 months typically.
- Traditional braces: $3,000–$6,000. Treatment 12–36 months depending on case.
(Exact prices vary a lot; get written estimates.)

If you want specific names and phone numbers now, tell me:
- Which Columbus (OH?) and a ZIP code
- Adult or child
- Any preferences (Invisalign only, budget, insurance)
I’ll pull 3–5 specific offices near you with phone numbers, short reasons to call each, and which to prioritize for Invisalign vs braces.
